solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Think Britain has terrible wet weather

parts.note: B is a standard abbreviation for Britain or British
a rainstorm is a spell of heavy, unpleasant wet weather

explanation.surface: Someone reflects gloomily on how awful the British climate is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Think' looks like an opening verb of the musing, but it is the definition, in the verb sense of pooling ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: To brainstorm is to think hard, generating ideas, often in a group session.

clue.text: Fast runner to run fast

definitions.meaning: Usain ..., the Jamaican sprinter and record holder

explanation.surface: A sprinter is described doing what sprinters do.
explanation.definitionFit: Usain Bolt is the world's most famous sprinter, and bolting is fleeing at speed.

clue.text: Reckon a number gets divided by one hundred

indicators.note: being divided by something means having it split you apart, so the hundred goes inside the other letters

parts.note: a count is a number or total
C is the Roman numeral for one hundred

explanation.surface: An arithmetic instruction: work out a number divided by a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: The division is physical, not arithmetic: C splits A COUNT after its A.
explanation.definitionFit: To account something so is to reckon or consider it that way.

clue.text: Partners who bid for a literary work

definitions.meaning: in bridge, the players sitting ... form one bidding partnership

explanation.surface: A pair bidding, perhaps at auction, for a valuable book.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridge seats are named by compass points, with opposite seats paired; Gaskell's novel contrasts England's regions.

clue.text: Coppers gained by redistribution of wealth

indicators.note: redistributing something shares it out differently, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Police seize wealth that someone has been redistributing, like a Robin Hood.
explanation.definitionFit: The law is an informal collective name for the police, as coppers are police officers.

clue.text: Grass skirts couple stitched up

indicators.note: to skirt is to go round the edge of, so the grass word surrounds the other

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: Skirts made of grass are worn by a couple who got stitched up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' reads as a noun for clothing; it is a verb meaning goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stitched up, such as a torn garment, has been mended.

clue.text: Blue drinks bottles where rubbish is left

indicators.note: to bottle something is to hold it inside, so the drinks word contains the rest

parts.note: to swallow a drink quickly in one go is to sink it; this word for that, plus S, wraps the rest
rubbish is left in the dump

explanation.surface: A sad soul drinks and the empties end up at the tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' looks like the empties; it is a verb meaning contains, putting IN THE DUMP inside DOWN...S.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue and being down in the dumps are both idioms for being depressed.

clue.text: Head's back in charge, firm about position

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the two short pieces before it are read backwards

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
to put is to position or place

explanation.surface: The boss has returned to work, and the company is reconsidering their role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head's back' reads as a manager returning; it is anatomy. 'about' turns ICCO into OCCI.
explanation.definitionFit: The occiput is the anatomical term for the rear part of the skull.

clue.text: Scientist's funny turn, penning article on stars

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the article goes inside
funny suggests something odd or out of order, so the letters of turn are mixed

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
the A-list is the set of top celebrities

explanation.surface: A scientist has a funny turn while writing about astronomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' suggests astronomy, but it means celebrities; 'funny' scrambles, 'penning' encloses, and 'on' sets the celebrity list after.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturalist is a scientist who studies the natural world, such as plants and animals.

clue.text: Writer about to conclude clear novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of clear take a new order

parts.note: RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A writer nears the end of a lucid novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the writer's book but signals the anagram LECAR; 'to conclude' puts RE at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: John le Carré was the English author of spy fiction such as Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy.

clue.text: Weaselly type of European given lash

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip or lash

explanation.surface: A sneaky continental character is flogged.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a member of the weasel family, so literally a weaselly type of animal.

clue.text: Like a thief with torch, say, implicated in crime

parts.note: a torch is an example of a light
to be fingered is to be identified to police as a culprit

explanation.surface: A burglar carrying a torch is caught up in a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Light-fingered describes someone prone to stealing, a pilferer or pickpocket.

clue.text: Manoeuvring has begun to secure duke one minor title

indicators.note: securing something holds it fast within, so the shuffled letters enclose the duke and one
manoeuvring means moving around, so the letters of has begun are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Political manoeuvring has started to win a duke a lesser title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manoeuvring' rearranges HAS BEGUN; DI goes inside to give SUBHEAD-ING.
explanation.definitionFit: A subheading is a secondary title placed under a main heading in a text.

clue.text: Strokes leopards around the middle

indicators.note: the letters needed sit at the centre of the word leopards, round its midpoint

explanation.surface: Someone pets big cats round their bellies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strokes' reads as caresses; it is the golf sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, par is the standard number of strokes expected for a hole or round.

clue.text: Chap's outstanding feature very gently covered in water

indicators.note: being covered in something means it surrounds you, so the water phrase encloses the music term

parts.note: Adam's ale is an old jocular name for water
PP, pianissimo, is the musical direction meaning very softly

explanation.surface: A man's best feature is gently rinsed with water.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam's ale is an old joke name for water, since Adam had nothing else to drink; 'covered in' puts the soft musical marking inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Adam's apple is the lump at the front of a man's throat, a literally protruding feature.

clue.text: Seeing daughter feeling animosity towards Cockney

indicators.note: London Cockney speech drops the initial H, so it is removed from the word

parts.note: hating means feeling animosity towards

explanation.surface: A girl is seeing someone while her family resents a Londoner.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys are East Londoners whose accent famously drops H, so HATING becomes ATING.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people seeing each other are romantically involved, which is dating.

clue.text: How many driving aids there are on the wagon

parts.note: in golf, a tee holds the ball up for a drive
a total is how many there are altogether

explanation.surface: A question about counting the aids for a vehicle driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving aids' suggests cars; it is golf. A tee total would be the count of tees.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the wagon is an idiom for abstaining from alcohol, as a teetotal person does.

clue.text: President's vehicle to get hot, storing energy

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

indicators.note: storing means holding something inside, so the heat verb contains the energy letter

parts.note: to burn is to get very hot
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: The presidential car overheats with its battery charged.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Van Buren was the eighth president of the United States; the possessive matches the apostrophe s.

clue.text: Anchor to remain beside sea

indicators.note: beside places the stay word next to the sea word, which comes first here

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the open sea
to stay is to remain

explanation.surface: A ship drops anchor to stay put by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anchor' reads as the ship's gear; here it means a support.
explanation.definitionFit: A mainstay is the chief support of something, which is what an anchor figuratively is.

clue.text: Ape is that thing found in India and China

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the pronoun goes into the other letters

parts.note: china means mate in Cockney rhyming slang, from china plate
it is a pronoun for that thing

explanation.surface: A question of whether an ape lives in India and China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country; in Cockney rhyming slang, London's word-swap game, china plate means friend. 'found in' sets the pronoun inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to imitate or mimic them.

clue.text: Might they be cool by river, beginning to soak?

definitions.text: Might they be cool by river, beginning to soak?

parts.note: hip means cool or fashionable
the Po is the major river of northern Italy

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that is taken from soak

explanation.surface: A question about animals cooling off by a river as they start to wallow.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippopotamuses keep cool by lying in rivers, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Item used to cook good stuff — it's very characterful!

parts.note: a pan is a cooking utensil
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: A cook praises a pan that makes characterful food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characterful' is literal: full of letters, as a sentence using every letter is.
explanation.definitionFit: A pangram is a sentence containing every letter of the alphabet, so it is full of characters.

clue.text: Year oddly in free hotel in the capital

indicators.note: in places the year letters inside the free word

parts.note: to rid is to free

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters, first and third, are taken from year

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A year staying free in a hotel in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Riyadh is the capital city of Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: One known for fighting got off without time

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the time letter is removed

parts.note: alit means got off, as from a bus or horse

explanation.surface: A fighter was acquitted without serving time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got off' suggests escaping punishment; it means dismounted.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali was the famous heavyweight boxing champion.

clue.text: Struggling pub calling for training targeted at issue

indicators.note: struggling suggests being in difficulty or disorder, so the letters of pub are jumbled

parts.note: ringing means calling on the phone

explanation.surface: A failing pub phones around for staff training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means offspring, so the definition is training given to children.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbringing is the raising and training of children, who are one's issue.

clue.text: Opening words of "Ode to a Manx Cat", perhaps, in this work

definitions.text: Opening words of "Ode to a Manx Cat", perhaps, in this work

parts.words: Opening words of "Ode to a Manx Cat", perhaps, in this work
parts.note: an ode traditionally opens with a vocative O addressing its subject, here a cat by its pet name; run together that gives a term for a creative work

explanation.surface: A poem addressed to a tailless cat from the Isle of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: Odes traditionally open with an address such as O followed by the subject; for a cat that gives O PUSS.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a creative work, especially a musical composition.

clue.text: Maybe Gary Lineker is a menace to the game!

definitions.meaning: Gary Lineker, England striker turned TV presenter, was a classic goal ..., scoring from close range

explanation.surface: A former footballer is accused of harming the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a poacher is an opportunist striker; in the country, someone who steals game.

clue.text: Show eg obstetrician medical procedure for delivery

parts.note: to air is to show or broadcast
an obstetrician is an example of a doctor, DR
OP is short for operation

explanation.surface: A TV programme follows a doctor through a birth procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivery' suggests childbirth with the obstetrician; it is supplies dropped from aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An airdrop is a delivery of supplies by parachute from an aircraft.

clue.text: Etonian PM partied energetically, covering this up

indicators.note: covering something up conceals it, so the answer lies concealed across the join of partied and energetically

explanation.surface: An Old Etonian prime minister partied hard and hushed it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering this up' sounds like a scandal being suppressed; it signals letters concealed in the clue's words.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Eden, educated at Eton College, was British prime minister from 1955 to 1957.
